t: Commissioning: the whole line, start to finish
html:
In the app

Guided mode’s last lesson is this chapter, and File → Load Reference Solution: Complete Bottle Line (15 steps) in another project is the answer key to compare against.

With all fifteen routines in place, MainRoutine is fifteen JSRs, S3_Index last. Logic → Verify Controller: 0 errors. Reset Sim. Then run this checklist, the one the program’s own test runs on every release:

  1. Run mode. Press Start. Run lamp on; Pack_HMI shows RUNNING; the belt steps and a bottle drops every stop.
  2. Within a minute bottles are filling at stop 7 (a large charge for large bottles, a small one for small) and capping at stop 10 (the magazine turns a pocket per cap).
  3. Every capped bottle leaves the labeler with a label, and the camera passes it; Label_Fault stays off and the inspection count climbs.
  4. Broken bottles are dropped into the shredder; the box conveyor brings a box, banded with hazard tape, under the chute; IN BOX counts up; the full box leaves and the next arrives; BOXES counts 1.
  5. Small bottles ride the incline to the divert conveyor and are counted on SMALL; large bottles run to the end and are counted on LARGE; SCRAP counts the broken ones. Both sizes are packed, four to a case and one size per case: CASES LARGE and CASES SMALL on Pack_HMI both climb, and no empty case is sent out.
  6. Nothing is lost (the simulator’s counters show no red lost) and the Simulator Log has no line about a bottle with nothing under it or nothing to land on.
  7. Supply_Tank falls to its low float, the red light flashes, the inlet opens, the level climbs. Every time it does, Mix_Tank has a batch ready and pumps it across; when the inlet closes, the kitchen tops itself up. Supply_Tank never stays below its low float.
  8. Dial 0010 on the thumbwheel; the line stops at ten large bottles; Enter clears; Start runs again.
  9. Alarm_Word stays 0 and the fault lamp dark for the whole run, including when you press Stop and Start at random moments.
  10. Each fault of chapter 28’s Run it, and a drive trip on Case_VFD, injected with Tools → Inject Machine Fault, is caught by the bit the table says, stops the line if it should, and clears with Clear Machine Faults, Reset and Start.

The regression runs that list on every release. If any line fails for you, the Simulator Log names the device, Monitor Tags shows the bit, and the matching lesson’s Run it says what should have happened. The finished template (File → New Project… → LogixPro-style Bottle Line) is the answer key; File → Export / Copy as Text… on both and compare. Appendix B is the complete listing and Appendix C the bit map. Save the project. You have built a bottling line from an empty floor and written every rung that runs it.
